github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGenerat.text: Follow Conventional Commits: begin the subject with one of these type prefixes followed by a colon and a space — chore:, docs:, feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:.
Use the imperative mood after the prefix (e.g. 'feat: add match expression', not 'feat: added match expression'). Keep the first line under 72 characters with no trailing period.
Limit each commit to one logical change. Add a body explaining the why when the change is non-trivial.

github.copilot.chat.reviewSelection.inst.text: Prioritise findings: correctness and security bugs first, then performance, then style. Surface logic errors, unhandled edge cases, resource leaks (missing RAII), and concurrency hazards before stylistic nits.

Check the selection against the matching guide in the instructions/ folder (for example cpp.instructions.md for C++) and flag deviations from its naming, const-correctness, error-handling, and formatting rules.
For each finding give the file and line, a severity (Bug, Security, Performance, or Style), why it matters, and a concrete fix.

github.copilot.chat.pullRequestDescripti.text: Start the PR title with a Conventional Commit prefix (chore:, docs:, feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:) matching the dominant change.

Structure the body with a short Summary (what changed and why), a bulleted list of notable changes, and a Testing section noting how it was validated (cmake build, ctest, and the Luma feature suites via scripts/run_luma_tests.py).
Note any cross-platform impact (Linux, macOS, Windows) and link related issues. Keep it factual and concise; omit sections that do not apply.
